headers.comment: Baseline security headers. None of these need a build step or cost a request; leaving them off is the default only because nobody set them.
Stops a browser guessing a served file is a different type than declared, which is the vector behind most 'uploaded a .txt that ran as JS' bugs.
Send the full referrer within the site, origin-only cross-site, nothing when downgrading to http.
This site asks for no device permissions, so it declines them all up front.
No reason for this site to be framed by anyone.
Two years, subdomains included. Safe here because the site is https-only.
Astro fingerprints everything in _astro/, so those URLs can never go stale. Cache them for a year and immutably.
Generated imagery is not fingerprinted, so it gets a day of browser cache and a week at the edge with revalidation rather than immutability.
The agent-readable routes and the PDF change with the content, so revalidate but serve instantly from the edge while doing it.
